source_text: Groupoids in functors on an arbitrary category

<STRUCT_0001>
We begin with generalities on groupoids in functors on an
arbitrary category. In the next section we will
pass to the category <MATH_0001>.
For clarity we shall sometimes refer to an ordinary groupoid,
i.e., a category whose morphisms are all isomorphisms, as a groupoid category.

Let <MATH_0001> be a category. The
<TEXTITOPEN_0001>category of groupoids in functors on <MATH_0002><TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
is the category with the following objects and morphisms.

<STRUCT_0004>

A groupoid in functors on <MATH_0001> amounts to the data of a functor
<MATH_0002>, and a morphism of groupoids
in functors on <MATH_0003> amounts to a morphism of the corresponding
functors
<MATH_0004> (where
<MATH_0005> is regarded as a 1-category).  However, for our
purposes it is more convenient to use the terminology of groupoids in functors.
In fact, thinking of a groupoid in functors as the corresponding functor
<MATH_0006>, or equivalently as the
category cofibered in groupoids associated to that functor, can lead to
confusion (Remark <REF_0001>).
